items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Bud Lawyer-Kaner; the name is introduced by the interviewer as part of a list of musicians in Alfred Lane's band.

ctx.x: Was for, you say from, you would say from Algiers up into West Wigo. All the funerals over there. None on this side. Because they used to play all that funerals. It seemed, I don't know, they had some agreement, some contracts in there with these organizations. See, these men did, you understand? And of course, had to hire them in case of the funerals. Now, me, well, of course, I never had no contract with none of them and no agreements with none of them. And if they died, they wanted my band, they wanted us to…

You see, this band, that's the first band that ever played on the air, over the air. W-O-W-L. You can hardly see them anymore. Who was the man? Alfred Lane. Alfred Lane, he had that, and Jimmy Cousins and Marlowe and Bud Lawyer-Kaner was with him.
Yeah, what play? Is this the same Marlowe that helped Nick LaRocca learn his...
